henry.title: Two Worlds in Three Sentences
henry.mission: Collect two describing words for Venus and two for Enceladus, then write 3 sentences that compare them, including one simile.
henry.done: Both word pairs are filled, and your 3 sentences are written.
words: a word that tells how something looks
a comparison that uses like or as

flow.title: Describing words on Venus
flow.teach:
A describing word tells how something looks. Example, about a playground, not about space: The playground was noisy and bright.

Drive on Venus. Pick two words that match what you see. You may use the bank or your own words: hazy, bright, pale, rough, smooth, dark, rocky, cracked.
pics: W A S D. Stop and look close, then far.
flow.sheet:
Venus place name:
Two words for how it looks: and

flow.title: Describing words on Enceladus
flow.teach: Do the same on the second world. A pale or bright look tells how it looks. It does not tell you what the ground is made of.
flow.sheet:
Enceladus place name:
Two words for how it looks: and

flow.title: Three sentences and one simile
flow.teach:
A simile compares two different things with like or as.

Example, still about a playground: The slide was as shiny as a spoon.

Write only 3 sentences. Use your words from Tasks 1 and 2.
flow.sheet:
On Venus, it looked and .
But on Enceladus, it looked and .
One place looked as as .

henry.challenge: Optional fourth sentence. NASA's Venus fact sheet lists thick carbon-dioxide air and an average temperature of 737 K (464 C). NASA's Enceladus page says it is an icy moon and the most reflective body in the solar system. Add one of those facts and write NASA next to it. Your three sentences stay about what you saw.
henry.adult:
Your setup time is not part of his 15 minutes. Open Regolith yourself. Press H and follow H. Do not overwrite a save. Land on a readable Venus name, then a readable Enceladus name. He uses only W A S D. Pause the timer while you switch. Both boys can share the landing.

Venus menu names from older visits included Venera 13 and Alpha regions, but use whatever readable name you see. Enceladus choices include Tiger stripes (Baghdad Sulcus), the circumpolar ridge belt, or Saturn-facing cratered plains. Do not require a jet, frost, or ice. A pale look is not proof of ice.

If a world will not load, he can use a NASA photo and write photo by that row. Sources for the optional fact: NASA Venus fact sheet (92 bars, about 96.5 percent carbon dioxide, 737 K) and the NASA Enceladus page (icy, most reflective body). Do not grade colors. No jump test. Skip Titan, Io, and Europa.

parentKey.assess: Score two look-words for each world and 3 sentences that follow the starters, with like or as in sentence 3. Words should match what he says he saw. Do not require the word ice. The NASA sentence is not scored.

items.a: A readable place name and two describing words tied to what he saw.
A readable place name and two describing words tied to what he saw.

Three sentences on their own lines. Example shape: On Venus, it looked dark and rough. But on Enceladus, it looked pale and smooth. One place looked as pale as a sheet of paper. Sentence 3 needs like or as.

frankie.title: Light, Dark, or Other
frankie.mission: Look at Venus and Enceladus, mark light, dark, or other, count what you point to, and write fog.
frankie.done: Both worlds are marked and counted, the words are matched, and you wrote fog.

flow.title: Two worlds
flow.teach: Grown-up, read aloud. He drives a little with W and points at things he chooses. Light, dark, or other are all fine.
pics: W to roll a little, then stop.
sheets: Venus. Circle: light / dark / other. I counted: ____
Enceladus. Circle: light / dark / other. I counted: ____
Stretch, only if you want it: add the two counts ____. Which had more? Venus / Enceladus / same

flow.title: Read and write fog
flow.teach: Grown-up, name the pictures first. The cloud is fog. The drop is wet. The fire is hot. Hot matches the fire picture. It is not a word for how the world looks.
sheets: Draw a line. Words: fog, wet, hot. Pictures: fire 🔥   fog 🌫️   wet drop 💧.

Circle every it: I see it. I like it.
Trace: I see it.
Write fog: __________

frankie.adult:
Same Venus and Enceladus landings as Henry. Hot is only the phonics picture of a fire. Do not ask him to say the planet looks hot.

When he circles it, a capital or a small letter both count.

parentKey.assess: Score both look circles, both counts, the word match, and writing fog. The add-and-compare line is optional. Other and same are acceptable answers.

items.a: Light, dark, or other, plus his count.
Light, dark, or other, plus his count.
Optional. The sum of his counts, and Venus, Enceladus, or same to match those counts.
fog to the cloud, wet to the drop, hot to the fire picture.
Both it words circled. He traces and writes fog.
